title: THE PHANTOM RE-SETTLING LAG -- the sqrt-2 sound response in a real merger: a second clock (the three-timescale hierarchy and the phantom-first re-alignment ordering)
question: after a merger, on what timescales do the four components re-attach to the baryonic centroid -- the phantom at R/c (light), the phantom condensate at t_sound = sqrt(2) t_dyn (sound), the gas at the shock crossing, the dust never -- and what re-alignment ordering (the observable timeline) distinguishes the sourced field from collisionless DM?

references.C01/B05: the sqrt-2 sound identity: t_sound/t_dyn = v_flat/c_s = sqrt(2) EXACTLY for the isothermal dark gas (c_s = sigma, v_flat = sqrt(2) sigma); Lean-certified (10 theorems, exit 0)

verdicts.V1: V1 [the three-timescale hierarchy, quantitative] in the Bullet (G110) the response ladder is: (a) PHANTOM at the LIGHT crossing tau_ph = R/c = 1.90 Myr (the sourced field's algebraic response; S6's zero-point, the ROUTE3 ~2-Myr line); (b) PHANTOM-CONDENSATE at its SOUND response t_sound = sqrt(2) x t_dyn = 621 Myr (B5/C01, c_s = sigma = 917 km/s, the SECOND clock -- the same phantom, re-arranging at c_s once sourced); (c) BARYONIC GAS at the shock/sound crossing t_gas ~ 481 Myr (c_s,gas = 1184 km/s via the G109 equipartition; shock sweep 121 Myr) -- the ~1e7-8 yr class; (d) DUST at the ballistic rate = never (t_relax/t_Hubble = 1e73.0-1e75.2).  THE HIERARCHY: tau_ph (2 Myr) << t_sound ~ t_gas (~1e8 yr) << t_dust (never): the phantom re-settles ~160x before the gas re-conditions (t_gas/tau_ph = 253), and the dust towers 1e70+ orders above the gas.
verdicts.V2: V2 [the re-alignment ordering] after a merger the framework predicts the PHANTOM re-attaches to the baryonic centroid FIRST (tau_ph = R/c = 1.90 Myr), the GAS later (the post-shock re-equilibration, t_gas ~ 481 Myr ~ 1e8 yr), the DUST NEVER.  The 'phantom-first' ordering is the sourced field's distinctive merger signature: the DARK-MASS centroid snaps back to the baryons on the light clock, before the gas even re-extends its hydrostatic support -- the exact opposite of CDM, where the collisionless dark lags and re-attaches on the dynamical/relaxation timescale (t_dark ~ t_dyn = 439 Myr) at or after the gas.  The observable sequence is the timeline phantom -> gas -> dust(never), C2.
verdicts.V3: V3 [the honest statement] the phantom's re-settling clock is the merge ordering that distinguishes the sourced field from collisionless DM: the registered falsifier is ANY merger showing the dark-mass offset persisting AS LONG AS / LONGER than the baryonic gas's own re-alignment (the CDM-like slow re-attachment, t_dark >= t_gas) -- that leaves no fast R/c baryon-tracking phantom.  The framework predicts t_ph = 1.90 Myr << t_gas = 481 Myr and agrees with a PERSISTENT dark offset only when it is collisionless dust (S6: the Bullet's 8-sigma offset is dust-carried, kinematically realizable, phantom bounded at f_ph <= 0.125).  WHAT IS AND ISN'T ESTABLISHED, stated exactly: (1) the Bullet alone does NOT demonstrate the phantom-first ORDERING -- its offset is dust, expected to persist, so it does not separate t_ph < t_gas from t_dark >= t_gas (S6 V3's shared-with-CDM offset); (2) the second clock (t_sound = sqrt(2) t_dyn) is a re-arrangement clock of the phantom once sourced -- it does NOT move the offset, which is the dust's; the phantom is zero-offset on BOTH its clocks (S6 C3); (3) the discriminating observation is a merger pair caught in the window between t_ph and t_gas (~2 Myr .. ~1e8 yr) where the gas is still disrupted but the phantom has re-attached -- the seconds-available prediction of the sourced field; (4) the thick-era dust-clock reading (G111 N-body, t_cross 82 Myr) and the sound-clock reading are the framework's two independent ways to discriminate, and both are falsifiable against the collisionless baseline.
